extracted.intended_audience: auditors performing single audits of non‑Federal entities under OMB Circular A-133 (states, local governments, Indian tribal governments, and non‑profit organizations)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for auditors to identify applicable compliance requirements for Federal programs, determine audit objectives, and design and perform tests of compliance (including cost allowability, indirect costs, activities allowed/unallowed, and internal control) under OMB Circular A-133. Covers use of the Supplement's matrix, Part 3 general requirements, and Parts 4/5 program‑specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix of Compliance Requirements — Y/shaded interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: How to use Part 2 matrix to identify which types of compliance requirements may apply to a program; each matrix box contains a 'Y' if the requirement may apply or is shaded if the program normally does not have activity subject to that requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'Y' indicates the type of compliance requirement may apply to the Federal program but may not apply at a particular non‑Federal entity (e.g., no activity subject to that requirement or not material). Auditor should exercise professional judgment to determine which 'Y' requirements need testing at a particular entity. If a requirement is shaded, it normally does not apply, but auditors must test it if evidence (e.g., grant agreement review or discussions with management) suggests it could have a material effect on a major program. Use Part 3 for general descriptions and suggested audit procedures and Parts 4/5 for program‑specific criteria; Part 6 (Internal Control) may assist in assessing control risk and designing tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to consider Part 3 and Parts 4/5 in every A-133 audit
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditors shall consider the compliance requirements and related audit objectives in Part 3 and Part 4 or 5 in every audit of non‑Federal entities under OMB Circular A-133, except program‑specific audits performed under an agency's program‑specific guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When deciding not to test a requirement, the auditor must conclude it either does not apply to the entity or noncompliance could not have a material effect on a major program. Descriptions in Parts 3, 4, and 5 are summaries; auditors should refer to referenced laws and regulations for complete requirements. Suggested procedures are guidelines; auditor judgment is necessary to determine sufficiency and whether additional procedures are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal Control — auditor assessment and testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditor must determine appropriate procedures to test internal control on a case‑by‑case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 3 does not prescribe suggested procedures to test internal control because of diversity among entities. The auditor should consider factors such as the entity's internal control, the compliance requirements, audit objectives for compliance, the auditor's assessment of control risk, and A-133's requirement to test internal control when designing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activities Allowed or Unallowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific program laws, regulations, and grant/contract provisions define which activities may or may not be funded under a program; objective is to ensure Federal awards were expended only for allowable activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audit Objective: Determine whether Federal awards were expended only for allowable activities. Suggested Audit Procedures: (1) Identify types of activities specifically allowed or prohibited by laws, regs, and agreements; (2) If allowability is determined from summary data, verify activities were allowable and transactions were properly classified and accumulated; (3) If determined from individual transactions, select sample transactions and verify allowability; (4) Be alert for large transfers of funds from program accounts that may have funded unallowable activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Compliance Requirements (matrix headings)
rubrics_metrics.description: List of common compliance requirement types that may apply to Federal programs (as presented in the matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types shown include: Activities Allowed or Unallowed; Allowable Costs/Cost Principles; Cash Management; Eligibility; Equipment and Real Property Management; Matching, Level of Effort, Earmarking; Period of Availability of Federal Funds; Procurement and Suspension and Debarment; Real Property Acquisition/Relocation Assistance; Reporting; Special Tests and Provisions; Program Income (and others as applicable). Use the matrix to determine which types may apply to a program and then consult Part 3 and Parts 4/5 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of OMB cost principles circulars
rubrics_metrics.description: Which OMB cost principles circulars apply to different types of non‑Federal entities administering Federal awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB Circular A-87 applies to States, local, and Indian tribal governments. OMB Circular A-21 applies to institutions of higher education and incorporates CASB standards and DS‑2 requirements. OMB Circular A-122 applies to non‑profit organizations (except certain nonprofits listed in Attachment C of A-122, which follow FAR commercial cost principles). Publicly‑owned hospitals and other medical care providers are exempt from OMB cost principles but subject to agency requirements (e.g., 45 CFR part 74, appendix E). Cost principles apply to all Federal awards received by the entity, whether direct or pass‑through.

rubrics_metrics.name: General criteria for allowability of costs (direct and indirect)
rubrics_metrics.description: The overarching standards that costs must meet to be allowable under Federal awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs must be: reasonable and necessary for performance and administration; allocable to Federal awards under cost principles or CAS standards; consistently treated per generally accepted accounting principles (a cost cannot be direct for one purpose and indirect for another in like circumstances); conform to limitations or exclusions in the circulars, Federal/State/local laws, sponsored agreements, or regulations; net of applicable credits; and documented in accordance with A-110 (nonprofits) or A-102 (governments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowability detailed criteria for transaction testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific criteria auditors should test when examining charges to Federal awards (detailed from 'Basic Guidelines').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When testing transactions, verify they: a) for state/local governments, are authorized/not prohibited by state/local laws; b) are approved by the Federal awarding agency if required; c) conform with allowability provisions of applicable cost principles and program limits; d) conform with allocability provisions; e) represent actual costs (not budgeted/projected); f) for fringe benefits, allocations are based on benefits received by employee classes; g) applied uniformly to Federal and non‑Federal activities; h) given consistent accounting treatment within and between periods; i) calculated in conformity with CAS, GAAP, or other required basis where applicable; j) not used to meet cost‑sharing requirements of other Federally‑supported activities; k) net of applicable credits (discounts, rebates, recoveries, etc.); l) not included both as a direct billing and as a component of indirect costs. Support by appropriate documentation (purchase orders, invoices, canceled checks, time and attendance) is required; salary/time and effort documentation requirements are described in applicable cost principles. Documentation may be electronic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect Costs — CAPs/IDCRPs and rate types
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for preparing, submitting, and using indirect cost allocation plans and indirect cost rate proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations must prepare CAPs (for States/local/tribes) or IDCRPs (for institutions and non‑profits) and submit to the Federal cognizant agency for indirect cost negotiation (or maintain on file if exempt). Three types of plans/proposals for governments: State/Local Governmentwide CAPs, Department or Local IDCRP, and Public Assistance CAPs. Indirect costs are accumulated at State/local‑wide and department/agency levels. Rate types: predetermined (not subject to adjustment except very unusual circumstances), fixed (differences carried forward as adjustments), and provisional/final (temporary until final rate established). Indirect cost proposals should be based on current financial data and audited statements; CAPs include narratives describing service centers and allocation methodologies and mathematical allocations to users. Differences between recovered and actual costs are carried forward or adjusted with cognizant agency approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure Statements (DS-2 and DS-1) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: When institutions must prepare and maintain cost accounting disclosure statements and related responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB Circular A-21 requires institutions of higher education receiving more than $25 million in Federal funding in a fiscal year to prepare and submit a DS‑2 describing cost accounting practices within six months after the end of the first fiscal year beginning after May 8, 1996 (or earlier if required by receipt of a CAS‑covered contract). Institutions must maintain an accurate DS‑2 and file amendments when disclosed practices change. Some non‑profits by contract may be subject to CAS and DS‑1 requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large research facilities construction cost review requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural and documentation requirements for institutions constructing large research facilities with substantial Federal use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For large research facilities (> $10 million) with 40%+ assignable space expected for Federal use, institutions must maintain an adequate review and approval process to ensure construction costs are reasonable. Review should address life cycle costs, unique research needs, special building needs, site preparation, environmental considerations, federal construction code requirements, and competitive procurement practices. Approval must include review by the institution's Board of Trustees or other independent entities. For facilities > $25 million with 50%+ Federal use, institutions must document review steps, include analysis and comparisons to relevant construction data (e.g., NSF biennial survey).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit objectives for direct and indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific objectives auditors should achieve when auditing allowability and allocation of direct and indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives include: 1) Direct charges to Federal awards were for allowable costs; 2) Charges to cost pools used in calculating indirect cost rates were for allowable costs; 3) For governments, charges to cost pools allocated to Federal awards through CAPs were for allowable costs; 4) Allocation methods conform to applicable cost principles/CAS and produce equitable distribution; 5) Indirect cost rates applied per approved rate agreements and billings result from approved rates applied to proper bases; 6) For governments, cost allocations follow CAPs approved by the Federal cognizant agency or plan on file; 7) Disclosure statements (DS‑1/DS‑2) represent actual practice consistently applied (where required); 8) Institution's review of large research facilities under construction was documented as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested audit procedures — general approach and directly associated costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on audit procedures to test direct charges and charges to cost pools or indirect cost rates, including treatment of unallowable costs and associated costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General procedures apply to direct charges and charges to cost pools. If auditor identifies unallowable costs, consider 'directly associated costs' (costs incurred solely as a result of incurring another cost — e.g., fringe benefits tied to payroll); when an unallowable cost is incurred, directly associated costs are also unallowable. Test a sample of transactions for conformance with the Basic Guidelines (see detailed criteria a‑l). For material charges from internal service/central service/pension or similar activities, verify charges are in accordance with applicable cost principles and consider procedures to validate allocation methods and supporting documentation.
